# Dataset Documentation

**No third-party dataset is redistributed in this repository.** Only synthetic data generated by this project is included.

## 1. Synthetic flow-feature samples (`datasets/samples/*.csv`)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Purpose | demos, CSV-upload testing, examples |
| Source | generated by `safeguard_pq.simulation` (seed 11, device `ECG-ICU-007`, 2 ticks after injection) |
| License | Apache-2.0 (part of this repository) |
| Type | **Synthetic** — not real network traffic |
| Files | `synthetic_benign`, `synthetic_syn_flood`, `synthetic_ddos_volumetric`, `synthetic_port_scan`, `synthetic_mqtt_malformed`, `synthetic_arp_spoofing` |
| Rows | 100 per file |
| Redistribution | allowed |

Schema (subset of CICIoMT2024 column names; values per flow record):

| Column | Meaning | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| `syn_flag_number`, `ack_flag_number`, `rst_flag_number`, `fin_flag_number` | TCP flag present (0/1) | — |
| `TCP`, `UDP` | protocol indicator (0/1) | — |
| `Rate` | packet rate | packets/s (synthetic scale) |
| `Tot size` | packet size | bytes |
| `Header_Length` | header length aggregate | bytes (CICIoMT semantics) |

Generation parameters per attack class are in `backend/src/safeguard_pq/simulation/catalog.py`. They imitate the
*shape* of CICIoMT2024 class statistics; they are not samples of it. Missing values: none.
Known bias: distributions are idealised and stationary.

## 2. Built-in scenarios (`backend/src/safeguard_pq/data/scenarios.json`)

Ten hand-written synthetic system descriptions. Patient names, MRNs and e-mail addresses are fictional; credentials are
generated at runtime and are invalid.

## 3. Regression fixtures (`backend/tests/fixtures/reference/`)

Three input/output pairs recorded from the v0 prototype in June 2026. Inputs are feature summaries of the first 100 rows
of CICIoMT2024 test files (aggregate statistics only, no raw records) and Synthea-generated synthetic patient names.

## 4. CICIoMT2024 (third party — not included)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Purpose | calibration/evaluation of traffic rules; optional simulator replay |
| Source | Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity (CIC), University of New Brunswick |
| URL | https://www.unb.ca/cic/datasets/iomt-dataset-2024.html |
| License / terms | as published by CIC; users must obtain the data from CIC and cite the dataset paper listed on the dataset page |
| Type | real traffic captured in a laboratory IoMT testbed (contains no patient data) |
| Used split | `WiFi_and_MQTT/attacks/CSV/test` (ARP spoofing, benign, MQTT malformed, recon port scan, TCP DDoS, TCP SYN DoS) |

Preparation: download the CSV test files into any folder and pass it to `benchmarks/traffic_rules_eval.py --data-dir`, or
set `REPLAY_DATA_DIR` for simulator replay. Splitting: the rules were tuned and evaluated on the test split only (no
held-out evaluation yet — see `docs/limitations.md`).

## 5. Synthea (third party — not included)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Purpose | synthetic EHR records for PHI-detection demos via CSV upload |
| Source | The MITRE Corporation — https://synthea.mitre.org/ |
| License | Apache-2.0 |
| Type | synthetic |
| Reference | Walonoski J. et al., "Synthea: An approach, method, and software mechanism for generating synthetic patients and the synthetic electronic health care record", JAMIA, 2018 |

Supported files: `patients.csv` (columns `Id`, `BIRTHDATE`, `FIRST`, `LAST`, …) and `conditions.csv` (`PATIENT`, `CODE`,
`DESCRIPTION`, …).

## Not supported on purpose

Credentialed clinical datasets (e.g. MIMIC, eICU) and any real patient data — their data-use agreements prohibit
redistribution, and the tool is not designed for real PHI.
